The mean value theorem states that if $f(x,y,z)$ is differentiable at each point on the line segment $\overset{―}{AB},$ then there exists a point $C\in \overset{―}{AB}$ with position vector $c$ such that

$$
f(b)-f(a)=∇f(c)·(b-a).
$$

Notice that $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}-{z}^{3}$ is differentiable at each point on the line segment $\overset{―}{AB}.$ So, we can apply the mean value theorem.

Substituting $a=⟨-1,0,1⟩$ and $b=⟨0,1,0⟩$ into the above expression, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0,1,0)-f(-1,0,1) & =∇f(c)\cdot (⟨0,1,0⟩-⟨-1,0,1⟩) \\ 0-0 & =∇f(c)\cdot ⟨1,1,-1⟩ \\ 0 & =∇f(c)\cdot ⟨1,1,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $∇f$ and evaluating at $c=⟨{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}⟩,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f & =⟨2x,0,-3{z}^{2}⟩ \\ ∇f(c) & =⟨2{c}_{1},0,-3{c}_{3}^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =∇f(c)\cdot ⟨1,1,-1⟩ \\ 0 & =⟨2{c}_{1},0,-3{c}_{3}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨1,1,-1⟩ \\ 0 & =2{c}_{1}+3{c}_{3}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $C$ lies on $\overset{―}{AB}.$ So, let's first find the equation of the line.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x-(-1)}{1} & =\frac{y-0}{1}=\frac{z-1}{(-1)} \\ x+1 & =y=1-z\end{aligned}
$$

Parametrizing the line, we get

$$
x=t-1\,\,y=t,\,z=1-t,\,0\le t\le 1.
$$

Since $c=⟨{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}⟩$ satisfies the equation of the line, we have

$$
{c}_{1}=t-1\,\,{c}_{2}=t,\,{c}_{3}=1-t.
$$

Substituting the above in the equation $2{c}_{1}+3{c}_{3}^{2}=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(t-1)+3(1-t)^{2} & =0 \\ (t-1)[2+3(t-1)] & =0 \\ (t-1)(3t-1) & =0 \\ t & =\frac{1}{3},\,1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we proceed to find the coordinates of the points that satisfy the mean value theorem.

- For $t=\frac{1}{3},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} & =\frac{1}{3}-1=-\frac{2}{3}, \\ {c}_{2} & =\frac{1}{3}, \\ {c}_{3} & =1-\frac{1}{3}=\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the coordinates of the first point $C$ are $(-\frac{2}{3},\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3}).$

- For $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} & =1-1=0, \\ {c}_{2} & =1, \\ {c}_{3} & =1-1=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the coordinates of the second point $C$ are $(0,1,0).$
